_status: PROPOSAL for parent language testing (Sept 7-18), not a locked identity. The decision brief forbids locking name, logo, palette or fonts before that testing. Everything here is versioned and swappable.
principles: The palette must survive being coloured on. Line art is the product; brand colour sits next to a child's crayon work and must not fight it.
Saudi green anchors the system but must not dominate every page.
Warm, curious, contemporary, respectful, child-capable. Never academic, preachy, touristy, ceremonial-only or babyish.
Arabic-first and genuinely bilingual. One type family carrying both scripts, not a Latin face with Arabic bolted on.
No flag, emblem, official mark, or any arrangement implying endorsement.

ink.use: All body text, line art, the default dark. A near-black with green in it, so it sits with the anchor rather than against it.

green.use: The anchor. Headings, primary buttons, the mark. Roughly 10-15% of any surface — never a full-bleed field behind artwork.

paper.use: The default ground everywhere. Warm, not white — it makes uncoated stock look intentional rather than cheap.

white.use: Cards, the printed sheet itself. Reserved, so it reads as 'the product' against paper.

terracotta.use: The second voice. Difficulty icons, talk-together prompts, highlights. Carries warmth the green cannot.

clay.use: Quiet fills, panel backgrounds, the calm behind a callout.

sky.use: The cool balance. Reef and sea content, informational states.

terracotta_text.use: Terracotta when it must carry words. The bright #C8763C is a graphic colour for icons, rules and marks; it only clears 2.5:1 on clay, so it never sets text on a warm ground.

muted.use: Tertiary text, captions, and the English line beneath every Arabic line. 4.70:1 on paper — the earlier #8B958F sat at 2.89:1 and failed everything.

rules: Never place brand colour behind line art. The child's colour must be the brightest thing on the page.
Green and terracotta never occupy equal area. One leads, one accents, and green leads by default.
Rose and sea are capsule and category colours, not brand colours. They must not appear on the masterbrand mark.
Every colour pairing used for text must clear the contrast table in the guidelines before it ships.
Terracotta has two values on purpose: the bright one is a graphic colour, the darker one is a text colour. Using the graphic value for words is the most likely way this palette fails an audit.

family.name: Tajawal
family.why: One family carrying Arabic and Latin with the same voice. The brief demands genuine bilingualism, and pairing an Arabic face with an unrelated Latin one is how 'Arabic added as decoration' happens in practice.

bilingual_rules: Arabic first, always: above, or to the right, never below the English.
English sits at 82-85% of the Arabic size and in a muted tone. It is the second reading, not a caption.
Never mirror an Arabic line into a Latin layout by flipping it. Set RTL properly and check on a device.
Outline all Arabic before print output. Shaping and diacritics break at RIP, not on screen.
Arabic-Indic numerals on the product; Latin numerals wherever a number must be machine-read.

logo.wordmark: Set in Tajawal 800, Arabic primary. The Latin transliteration sits beneath at 40% of the Arabic size, letterspaced, in muted tone.
logo.mark: A tear-out corner enclosing an open square — the page and the space the child fills. Drawn on an 8-unit grid so it holds at 16px.
logo.clearspace: One cap-height of the Arabic wordmark on all four sides. Nothing enters it, including the edge of the sheet.
misuse: Do not place the mark on artwork, or on any surface a child colours.
Do not recolour the mark outside ink, palm green, or reversed to paper.
Do not stretch, rotate, outline, add effects, or lock it to another logo.
Do not use the Latin wordmark alone in Saudi-facing material.
Do not set the mark beside any official symbol, emblem or flag.

geometry.grid: 8px base. Print grid 12mm safe margin on A4, per the printer brief.
